thread:
maria: quick heads-up — on canary host g4dn-heavy-07 I see a recurring tail-latency bump when FlashAttention + paged-KV are both enabled and the continuous batcher slices into a lot of tiny seqs. repro attached below.

jon: can you paste the raw p99s and a sample request shape? curious if it's seq-length or kv-page thrashing.

maria: p99 went from ~42ms -> ~210ms for some requests during a short window. most affected are mixes of 8-20 token requests interleaved with occasional 512-token warmups. sample trace: `batch=[8,12,512,9,10,...]` where 512 is a background long run.

kevin: that smells like a prefetch/eviction dance on paged-KV. FlashAttention kernel switch is cheap for long sequences but for tiny slices we might be paying kernel-launchs + KV page faults. did you capture `perf` counters?

maria: yup — attached perf counters gist (short):
```
cycles:u  2.1e9
L1-dcache-loads 1.9e7
page_faults  13
context-switches  0
gpu_kernel_launches  4823
```
not huge page faults overall but spikes align with the p99 tail.

anya: can we try forcing the batcher to colocate similar seq-lens (slice-aware grouping) and re-run? iirc we have a bias option in the continuous-batcher config.

jon: good call. also try toggling the FlashAttention fast-path heuristic to avoid kernel swaps for tiny sequences. we patched a gating flag last quarter: `--flash-kernel-threshold=64`. set to 128 to bias longer kernel.

maria: ran two quick tests:
1) slice-aware grouping on -> p99 stabilized to ~55ms, p50 unchanged
2) set `--flash-kernel-threshold=128` -> p99 ~60ms but CPU side kernel-launchs dropped 18%
so both helped.

kevin: interesting. did you capture KV cache miss stats? if the batcher groups tiny sequences it reduces interleaving with the 512s and avoids paged-KV churn.

maria: KV page evictions per minute: baseline 120 -> grouping 14 -> kernel-threshold change 40. grouping wins.

perf-bot: quick note — added a perf job comparing 3 configurations to the flaky-canary dashboard: grouping-only, kernel-threshold-only, both. link: https://perf.redwood/reports/1963012345

jon: actionable plan:
- make slice-aware grouping the default for low-token workloads (config flag + conservative hysteresis)
- keep `--flash-kernel-threshold` as a tunable but set default to 96 while we gather more data
- add a small prefetch window for paged-KV when a long sequence is detected in-flight to avoid eviction thrash

anya: also add a microbenchmark that simulates interleaved [8..20] + occasional 512 warmups so CI can catch regressions. put perf regression alerts on p99 > 2x baseline.

maria: i'll open a PR with the config change + microbench and push the perf job link. quick snippet of the microbench harness i used:
```
for i in range(10000):
  if random() < 0.01:
    send(seq=512)
  else:
    send(seq=random_choice([8,9,10,12,16,20]))
```
results saved to `s3://redwood-perf/canary/1963012345/`

kevin: solid. also add a tiny telemetry event from the batcher that reports "slice_grouping_enabled" and average slice size so we can monitor rollout impact.

maria: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:

jon: awesome. follow-up in this thread once the PR is up. if grouping causes any throughput regressions we'll roll back and iterate.

maria: PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/8321 — includes tests + perf job. tagging @anya for CI infra notes.

anya: taking a look, CI infra tweak needed for the microbench to run under 30m but i can pare it down.

perf-bot: job completed: grouping-only shows p99 down 3.8x vs baseline, throughput -0.6%. kernel-threshold-only shows p99 down 2.1x, throughput -0.1%. both combined similar to grouping-only.

maria: sweet. rolling canary to 25% with telemetry on. will report back in 4h.

jon: thanks. keep an eye on cross-tenant KV noise, might need tenant isolation tweak if we see noisy neighbors.

maria: noted — will monitor.
